name: Francoist Spain

flag.description: Horizontal stripes of red, a double-width yellow and red, with a coat of arms on the yellow: the shield of Spain held by the black Eagle of Saint John, between the Pillars of Hercules and beneath a scroll reading "Una, Grande, Libre".
flag.symbolism: The Eagle of Saint John and the yoke and arrows on the arms were taken from the badges of the Catholic Monarchs, Ferdinand and Isabella; the motto means "One, Great, Free".

hook: Under Franco, Spain's red-yellow-red flag carried a large black eagle spreading its wings behind the shield; today's flag has a smaller crowned shield and no eagle.
trivia: A modified eagle design was adopted in 1977, and the eagle was dropped in 1981, when Spain's present coat of arms was introduced.
The red-yellow-red stripes go back to a naval ensign chosen by King Charles III in 1785.
